Anguilla is a zero-tax jurisdiction. There is no income tax, capital gains tax, estate tax, or other form of direct taxation on individuals, regardless of residence status.

figures.finding: Anguilla levies no income tax on individuals, resident or not; the Inland Revenue Department's list of the taxes and laws it administers carries none.

figures.finding: From 1 January 2026 social security is 11.5% of wages, 5.75% deducted from the employee and 5.75% from the employer, up to a ceiling (EC$7,000 a month per Deloitte; the Board says to enquire); a self-employed person pays 8% of a weekly income chosen from categories (EC$200 to EC$1,250 in the Board's example).
figures.applies: Employees and self-employed persons insured with the Anguilla Social Security Board

sources.said: Effective January 1 st 2026 , Employers are entitled to deduct 5.75% of an employees earnings and match with their own portion of 5.75% up to the relevant contribution ceiling stipulated by law.

The amount of contribution payable by the self-employed person for each contributory week in respect of his employment shall be 8% of the weekly income elected by him/her … Category Weekly Income EC$ Weekly Contritbution EC$ A 1250.00 100.00 B 1000.00 80.00 C 800.00 64.00 D 600.00 48.00 E 400.00 32.00 F 200.00 16.00
On or after January 1st, 2027: Employees will contribute 6% and employers will contribute 6%, a combined total contribution of 12%.
Both the employer and employee contribute 5.75% of an employee’s earnings, up to XCD 7,000 per month, to social security.

figures.finding: The Universal Social Levy takes 3% of gross pay from employees earning over EC$2,000 a month, matched by the employer on pay up to EC$12,000 a month; a self-employed person pays 6% of gross earnings once they exceed EC$2,000 a month; returns are due within 10 days of the month's end.

sources.said: The Universal Social Levy (FKA Interim Stabilization Levy) also referred to as USL is a 3% levy on the gross salary or wages of all employees earning over EC$2,000.00 per month. The employer shall match the levy of 3% on the employee’s amount of remuneration or payment not exceeding EC$12,000.00 of an employee’s salary per month. Self-employed persons are required to pay 6% on their gross earnings once it exceeds EC$2,000.00 per month.

figures.finding: No income tax is withheld from pay or fees; the employer deducts only the social security and Universal Social Levy shares.

sources.said: There are no withholding taxes in Anguilla.

figures.finding: A non-resident performer, writer or director pays no income tax or withholding in Anguilla.

sources.said: There is no income tax, capital gains tax, estate tax, or other form of direct taxation on individuals, regardless of residence status. … There are no withholding taxes in Anguilla.

figures.finding: With no income tax, authors' fees and royalties are untaxed as income.

sources.said: There are no withholding taxes in Anguilla.

figures.finding: Since 1 August 2025 a service fee bears the General Services Tax at 13%; a service provider must register once taxable supplies reach EC$300,000 in 12 months (promoters of public entertainment must register whatever their revenue, per Deloitte).

sources.said: The General Services Tax is a tax on services. … General Services Tax came into force on August 1st 2025.

there shall be levied and paid a tax known as the General Services Tax, at a positive rate of 13% on the value of … made taxable supplies the total value of which equals or exceeds the amount of EC$300,000

Certain businesses are required to register for GNST regardless of annual revenue, including auctioneers, short-term accommodation providers, promoters of public entertainment, and state and statutory bodies.
